task.title: Review a churn model's results and spot what is wrong
task.brief: You get the summary of a churn model built by a junior colleague (see material). In 20-30 minutes, write short answers to three questions. 1) Work out precision and recall for the churn class from the table, and say whether 97% accuracy is a good sign here. 2) List the problems you see in how the model was built (features, split) and explain why each matters. 3) Recommend what to change before the retention team uses it, and how you would judge success. Show your working; plain sentences are fine, no code is needed.
task.material:
Churn model for a prepaid mobile operator (predict: will the customer leave in the next 30 days?)

Data: 120,000 customers, Jan-Sep 2026. Churn rate 6%.
Split: rows shuffled randomly, 80% train / 20% test.

Features used:
 tenure_months, avg_monthly_recharge_inr, data_gb_last_30d, calls_to_care_last_30d,
 days_since_last_recharge, port_out_request_flag, state, plan_type

Results on the test set (24,000 customers, 1,440 churners):
                 Predicted churn   Predicted stay
 Actual churn          1,296             144
 Actual stay             576          21,984

Accuracy 97.0%. Top feature by importance: port_out_request_flag (62%).
Note from ops: port_out_request_flag is set when the customer submits a number-porting request,
which is usually 1-3 days before they leave.

Business plan: the retention team can call 2,000 customers a month and offer a ₹99 data pack.
key_points: Accuracy is misleading with a 6% churn rate; a model predicting 'stay' for all gets 94%
port_out_request_flag is leakage or too late to act on: it appears days before leaving
Random shuffle on time-ordered data; use a time-based split (train earlier months, test later)
Retrain without the leaky feature and re-check metrics
Evaluate precision or lift in the top 2,000 to match the call capacity
Measure success with a holdout or control group: retained customers and revenue vs ₹99 offer cost

rubric.label: Correct numbers
rubric.guide: 0 = wrong or missing calculations, 3 = one metric right or minor slips, 5 = precision and recall right with working

rubric.label: Finds the real problems
rubric.guide: 0 = no issues found, 3 = spots leakage or the split but not both, 5 = leakage, split and misleading accuracy all explained

rubric.label: Fits the business use
rubric.guide: 0 = ignores the call team, 3 = generic advice, 5 = ties metric to top 2,000 calls and proposes a control group

rubric.label: Clear explanation
rubric.guide: 0 = hard to follow, 3 = understandable with gaps, 5 = short, clear reasons a manager could follow
